  <requirement id="R51">

    <spec_quote>Set localName to tagName in ASCII lowercase.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R52">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>trustedTypes.getPropertyType() must default elementNs to the HTML namespace when elementNs is null or an empty string.</description>
    <spec_quote>If elementNs is null or an empty string, set elementNs to HTML namespace.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R53">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>trustedTypes.getPropertyType() must return the expected Trusted Type interface name ("TrustedHTML", "TrustedScript", or "TrustedScriptURL") for known sink properties on matching element interfaces, and null when no matching sink property is found.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. Let expectedType be null.
    5. Find the row in the following table, where the first column is "\*" or interface’s name, and property is in the second column.
       If a matching row is found, set expectedType to the interface’s name of the value of the third column.

       | Element | Property name | TrustedType |
       | --- | --- | --- |
       | `HTMLIFrameElement` | "srcdoc" | `TrustedHTML` |
       | `HTMLScriptElement` | "innerText" | `TrustedScript` |
       | `HTMLScriptElement` | "src" | `TrustedScriptURL` |
       | `HTMLScriptElement` | "text" | `TrustedScript` |
       | `HTMLScriptElement` | "textContent" | `TrustedScript` |
       | "\*" | "innerHTML" | `TrustedHTML` |
       | "\*" | "outerHTML" | `TrustedHTML` |
    6. Return expectedType.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R54">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>trustedTypes.getAttributeType() must normalize the tagName argument to ASCII lowercase.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Set localName to tagName in ASCII lowercase.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R55">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>trustedTypes.getAttributeType() must normalize the attribute argument to ASCII lowercase.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. Set attribute to attribute in ASCII lowercase.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R56">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>trustedTypes.getAttributeType() must default elementNs to the HTML namespace when elementNs is null or an empty string.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. If elementNs is null or an empty string, set elementNs to HTML namespace.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R57">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>trustedTypes.getAttributeType() must convert an empty string attrNs argument to null.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. If attrNs is an empty string, set attrNs to null.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R58">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>trustedTypes.getAttributeType() must return the expected Trusted Type interface name when attributeData is found for the element, attribute, and attribute namespace, and null otherwise.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. Let expectedType be null.
    7. Set attributeData to the result of [get trusted type data for attribute](#get-trusted-type-data-for-attribute①) algorithm, with the following arguments:

       * interface as element
       * attribute
       * attrNs
    8. If attributeData is not null, then set expectedType to the interface’s name of the value of the fourth member of attributeData.
    9. Return expectedType.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R59">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When allowed by CSP, trustedTypes.createPolicy() must return a new TrustedTypePolicy object whose name property is set to the given policyName.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. Let policy be a new `TrustedTypePolicy` object.
5. Set policy’s `name` property value to policyName.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R60">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>trustedTypes.createPolicy() must capture the createHTML, createScript, createScriptURL, and createParserOptions callbacks from the provided policyOptions dictionary at policy creation time.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. Set policy’s [options](#trustedtypepolicy-options) value to «[
   "createHTML" -> options["`createHTML`"],
   "createScript" -> options["`createScript`"],
   "createScriptURL" -> options["`createScriptURL`"],
   "createParserOptions" -> options["`createParserOptions`"]
   ]».</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R61">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Creating a policy with the name "default" must set trustedTypes.defaultPolicy to the newly created policy.</description>
    <spec_quote>7. If the policyName is `default`, set the factory’s [default policy](#trustedtypepolicyfactory-default-policy) value to policy.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R62">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling createHTML, createScript, createScriptURL, or createParserOptions on a TrustedTypePolicy must invoke the corresponding callback with the input value followed by all additional variadic arguments.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Let args be « value ».
6. Append each item in arguments to args.
7. Let policyValue be the result of invoking function with
   args and `"rethrow"`.
8. Return policyValue.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R63">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling createHTML, createScript, or createScriptURL on a TrustedTypePolicy must stringify the callback's return value and return a new instance of TrustedHTML, TrustedScript, or TrustedScriptURL respectively with its associated data set to that string.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. Let dataString be the result of stringifying policyValue.
5. If policyValue is null or undefined, set dataString to the empty string.
6. Return a new instance of an interface with a type
   name trustedTypeName, with its associated data value set to dataString.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R64">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When a named policy's createHTML, createScript, or createScriptURL callback returns null or undefined, the returned Trusted Type object must have its associated data set to the empty string.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. If policyValue is null or undefined, set dataString to the empty string.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R65">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When invoking a policy's createParserOptions callback, the options dictionary passed to the callback must contain runScripts (defaulting to false) and, if a sanitizer option was provided, a newly configured Sanitizer instance under the sanitizer key.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Let runScriptsInput be dictionary["runScripts"], with default false.
2. Let argument be the ordered map «[ "runScripts" → runScriptsInput ]».
3. Let sanitizerInput be the result of [getting a sanitizer](#get-a-sanitizer-from-dictionary) from realm and dictionary.
4. If sanitizerInput is not null, set argument["sanitizer"] to sanitizerInput.
5. Return argument.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R66">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When converting a parser options dictionary's sanitizer member into a Sanitizer instance, the implementation must accept the "default" SanitizerPresets value (using the built-in safe default configuration), a Sanitizer instance (using its configuration), or a SanitizerConfig dictionary.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. If sanitizerInput is a `SanitizerPresets`:

   1. Assert: sanitizerInput is `"default"`.
   2. Set configuration to the built-in safe default configuration.
5. Otherwise, if sanitizerInput is a `Sanitizer`:

   1. Set configuration to sanitizerInput’s configuration.
6. Otherwise, if sanitizerInput is a `SanitizerConfig`:

   1. Set configuration to sanitizerInput.
7. Assert: configuration is not null.
8. Let sanitizer be a new `Sanitizer` in realm.
9. Configure sanitizer given configuration and true.
10. Return sanitizer.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R67">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling createParserOptions on a TrustedTypePolicy must return a new TrustedHTMLParserOptions instance whose sanitizer configuration is copied from the callback's returned dictionary and whose runScripts is set to the returned runScripts value (defaulting to false).</description>
    <spec_quote>2. Let sanitizerConfig be the result of
      [getting a sanitizer configuration](#get-a-sanitizer-config-copy-from-dictionary)
      from policy’s relevant realm and policyValue.
   3. Let runScripts be policyValue["runScripts"] with default false.
   4. Return a new instance of `TrustedHTMLParserOptions` in policy’s relevant realm with its
      [sanitizer configuration](#trustedhtmlparseroptions-sanitizer-configuration) set to sanitizerConfig, and its
      [runScripts](#trustedhtmlparseroptions-runscripts) set to runScripts.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R68">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>For HTML parsing sinks, if compliant parser options resolve to a TrustedHTMLParserOptions instance, the sink must parse the stringified input using those options directly without requiring TrustedHTML or invoking createHTML.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If documentType is `"html"`:

   1. Set compliantOptions to the result of calling [get trusted type compliant parser options](#get-trusted-type-compliant-parser-options), passing global, options, false, sink, and optionsFromAuthor.

      Note: Sinks that construct options themselves, rather than taking them from the author, pass false for optionsFromAuthor.
      For example, `createContextualFragment()` sets `runScripts` to true.
   2. If compliantOptions is an instance of `TrustedHTMLParserOptions`, return (stringified input, compliantOptions).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R69">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>For XML parsing sinks, or for HTML parsing sinks when compliant parser options are not a TrustedHTMLParserOptions instance, the sink must obtain a TrustedHTML-compliant string via get trusted type compliant string.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Let compliantHTML be the result of calling [get trusted type compliant string](#get-trusted-type-compliant-string), passing `TrustedHTML`, global, input, sink, and `"script"`.
4. If the algorithm threw an error, rethrow the error.
5. Return (compliantHTML, compliantOptions).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R70">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When an input passed to an injection sink is already an instance of the sink's expected Trusted Type, the sink must accept and use the stringified input directly without invoking the default policy.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If input is an instance of expectedType, return stringified
   input and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R71">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When no CSP require-trusted-types-for directive matches the sink group, passing a string to an injection sink must succeed and use the stringified input directly without invoking the default policy.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. Let requireTrustedTypes be the result of executing [Does sink type require trusted types?](#does-sink-type-require-trusted-types) algorithm,
   passing global, sinkGroup, and true.
3. If requireTrustedTypes is `false`, return stringified input and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R72">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When Trusted Types are required for a sink group and a plain string is passed to an injection sink, the default policy's corresponding create* callback must be invoked with the stringified input, expected Trusted Type name, and sink name.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Let policyValue be the result of executing [get trusted type policy value](#get-trusted-type-policy-value), with the following arguments:

   * defaultPolicy as policy
